title: The arithmetic of sampling static quantum disorder: exact aliases, finite witnesses, and clock robustness
abstract: Whether a dephasing experiment can exclude static Hamiltonian disorder depends on the arithmetic of its measurement times. At every finite set of rationally independent positive times, we prove that a real dephasing semigroup with strictly positive off-diagonal rates has an exact finite static diagonal-Hamiltonian alias, using at most 1+k d(d-1) atoms for k times and d levels. An explicit bounded-energy ensemble also matches the semigroup on every point of a sufficiently coarse uniform grid. Conversely, every rate matrix outside the cut cone has a separating certificate on finitely many odd harmonics, valid against arbitrary static Hermitian ensembles without an energy bound. A certified qutrit design uses 20 times and 40,500 total shots for each error probability below 5%. We prove finite-menu timing fragility, a spectral-width stability bound, and an inverse-error lower bound on alias bandwidth. Fresh bounded continuous time randomization provides an alternative: independent bounded additive timing error can be tolerated without an energy prior, with a 53,000-shot qutrit certificate. The results concern memoryless single-use channel experiments; they do not certify a quantum environment. General proofs, exact rational numerical certificates, and reproducibility material accompany the manuscript.
